newsitem.title: USA: West Virginia militia member pleads guilty.
newsitem.headline: West Virginia militia member pleads guilty.

text.p: A West Virigina militia member pleaded guilty Thursday to a single count of conspiring to unlawfully manufacture explosives last year, federal prosecutors said.
They said Jack Phillips during a Mountaineer Militia meeting in May 1996 told an FBI informant he could get various explosives, including powerful plastic explosives.

Phillips agreed to prepare a "shopping list" of equipment and chemicals needed to make the explosives, the prosecutors said. He then provided a leader of the militia group with a list of laboratory equipment.

In September, Phillips reviewed a catalogue and identified several pieces of equipment and the chemicals necessary to manufacture the explosives, the prosecutors said. Some equipment was delivered to his home in September and October.

As part of the plea deal, Phillips, 58, faced a maximum of five years in prison when sentenced, U.S. Attorney William Wilmoth said. Phillips, who remained in home detention, became the second of seven defendants who have pleaded guilty.

The seven were indicted in November on charges that included plotting to plant bombs at the FBI's national fingerprint centre in Clarksburg, W.Va. But officials acknowledged the plot was broken up long before the plot could be carried out and that the facility never was in any danger.
The guilty plea was entered before a federal judge in Wheeling, W.Va. The Justice Department made available a copy of Wilmoth's news release annnouncing the guilty plea.
